business.title: An optimized majority-feedback QCA D-latch and SET/RESET-enabled SRAM cell for compact, low-latency nanoelectronic memory design
business.description: Quantum-dot cellular automata is a contender to replace the scaling of semiconductor technology as it hits physical limits of complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology, with its ability to switch faster, take up less space and consume less power. In this study, the design and functional verification of compact QCA data latch circuit and a memory cell suitable for SRAM operation are presented, which are designed, implemented and simulated in the QCA designer (QCAD) 2.0.3 software. The main contribution is a single-layer 14-cell D-latch with a 0.007 µm2 footprint, reducing the layout area, latency and QCA cost compared with a similar design previously reported in the literature. Another 15-cell variant is proposed, incorporating SET and RESET control, for SRAM-type applications, reducing peak energy dissipation by approximately 22% from the 14-cell baseline. The circuits are found to be compact, low-latency circuits for next-generation nanoelectronics memory and different logic circuit design applications with reduced power dissipation. The power dissipation and polarization map of proposed circuits are implemented in QCAPro Software.

science.title: Beyond the food tray: linking school nutrition and feeding programmes to student health and academic outcomes through health literacy and mental health
science.description: School nutrition and feeding programmes are pivotal in addressing both public health and educational challenges, yet their multidimensional impacts remain underexplored in resource-constrained settings. Guided by the Health-Promoting Schools (HPS) framework, this study examined the relationships between s°chool nutrition and feeding programmes, students’ self-reported physical health, and academic performance, with health literacy and mental health as potential mediators. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among pupils in basic schools, comprising primary and junior high levels, using standardised questionnaires. Data were analysed with structural equation modelling (SEM). The findings indicate that feeding programmes are positively associated with students’ self-reported academic performance, with health literacy and mental health acting as indirect pathways. Health literacy was also found to mediate the relationship between feeding programmes and students’ perceived physical health. Effect size analysis suggested that these associations were stronger in disadvantaged communities. In conclusion, school feeding initiatives may function as dual-impact strategies linked to both health (SDG 3) and education (SDG 4). Policymakers are encouraged to integrate meal provision with health education to improve students’ well-being and learning experiences in resource-constrained contexts.
